questions.question: Explain why one third is bigger than one fifth, using the fun run route.
questions.expected_answer: The route is the same length for both runners. Cut into 3 equal parts, each part is longer than when it is cut into 5 equal parts. So one third of the route is longer than one fifth, and the runner on one third has run further.

questions.question: Compare 5/8 with 3/8, and 2/3 with 2/5, and say which rule you used each time.
questions.expected_answer: 5/8 is bigger than 3/8: the bottoms are the same, so the parts are the same size and more parts win. 2/3 is bigger than 2/5: the tops are the same, so there are 2 parts each and thirds are bigger than fifths, so the smaller bottom wins.

questions.question: Order 3/4, 1/5, 1/2 and 3/8 from smallest to biggest and explain your method.
questions.expected_answer: Group them: 1/5 and 3/8 are less than a half, because 1 is less than half of 5 and 3 is less than half of 8; 1/2 is a half; 3/4 is more than a half. On the wall 1/5 is less than 3/8. The order is 1/5, 3/8, 1/2, 3/4.
